analysis.investment_thesis: Campus is India's dominant mass-market sports footwear brand with genuine India consumption tailwinds, but at P/E 55.7x the price is demanding far more growth than the business is currently delivering — revenue grew just 10% in FY25 and earnings at ₹121 Cr are barely above 2023's ₹117 Cr. The story exists, but the price is wrong.
key_strengths: India's #1 mass-market sports shoe brand — strong consumer-facing moat in value segment with high brand recall
Capital-efficient franchise: ROE 29.5%, ROCE 31.8%, and consistent positive FCF (₹176 Cr in FY25)
Improving FCF conversion (₹264 Cr in FY24, ₹176 Cr in FY25) with D/E a manageable 0.48
key_risks: Growth deceleration is the core problem — revenue went from +24% (FY23) to -2.4% (FY24) to just +10% (FY25); not a 55x P/E story
Margin erosion: EBITDA margin fell from 20.4% (FY22) to 14.9% (FY24) with only partial recovery to 16.3% in FY25; operating leverage not materializing
PEG is deeply unattractive — using forward P/E of 42.6x against even an optimistic 25% earnings growth gives PEG ~1.7; Lynch wants PEG <1.0
red_flags: Revenue flat-to-declining over FY23–FY25 (₹1,484 Cr → ₹1,448 Cr → ₹1,593 Cr) while valuation priced for a fast-grower
Operating income collapsed from ₹242 Cr (FY22) to ₹143 Cr (FY24) — a 41% drop — while revenue grew 21% over the same period; cost structure worsened materially
Earnings recovery in FY25 (₹89 Cr → ₹121 Cr, +36%) is a bounce off a weak base, not proof of a new growth trajectory
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Campus has the bones of a Lynch-style consumer niche dominator — I can walk into any tier-2 Indian city and see those shoes everywhere, and that's exactly the kind of grassroots brand strength I love. The India sports & athleisure wave is real, ROE at 29.5% is genuinely impressive, and the debt is not alarming. But investing is about the price you pay for the story, and at P/E 55.7x I need 35%+ consistent earnings growth to even break even on a PEG basis. The numbers don't support that: revenue compounded just ~7% from FY22 to FY25 (₹1,194 Cr to ₹1,593 Cr), and operating margins compressed 600 bps over the same period despite scale gains.

The FY25 recovery looks encouraging in isolation — net profit +36% YoY, EBITDA ₹259 Cr — but this is largely a normalization from a weak FY24, not evidence of an accelerating business. A Lynch "fast grower" needs to be demonstrably expanding its runway: new geographies, new categories, channel wins. I'd want to see two or three consecutive years of 20%+ revenue growth and margin expansion before paying 42-55x earnings. At ₹200 or below — implying a P/E around 40x on FY25 earnings — the risk/reward becomes more interesting. Right now, the price is running way ahead of the story.
